newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening higher, limited gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening higher, limited gains.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open higher on Monday, but analysts said the session's gains would be limited as bonds remained under pressure.
"I think we're going to open on the upside, but gains will be limited and the risk is for a slide back," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
She said Standard & Poor's September Futures contract was up slightly, boding well for a positive U.S. start, but upside potential was limited by weaker bonds.
Trading was expected to be quiet as many market players took a break ahead of Canada's national holiday on Tuesday.
"(So) today's activity can't be taken too seriously because volume is going to be low," Beattie said.
Toronto stocks finished Friday on a softer note, pressured by dropping precious mineral and bank sectors as investors shed issues before quarter-end.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index dipped 27.25 points to close at 6426.40.
In economic news, Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.8 percent in April after falling 0.2 percent (revised from 0.3 percent) in March, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast a rise of 0.6 percent on average for April.

U.S. treasuries drifted slightly lower early on Monday in light trade. Markets were preparing for a short week with the U.S. national holiday on Friday, with a big calendar of economic news, including the rate-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting July 1-2.

* Workers at Inco Ltd's Sudbury, Ontario operations ratified a new three-year labor deal on Saturday, ending a 26-day strike against the nickel giant. Workers were expected to return to work late in July after a scheduled three-week maintenance shutdown of the operations.
* In other labor news, workers at Bombardier Inc's de Havilland unit ratified a new three-year deal on Saturday, averting a strike at the Downsview, Ontario plant.
